projects.title: Die Kalandraka Weglampen
projects.bodytext_html:
Custom made path illumination for the climbing refuge, Kalandraka, in Rodellar, Spain. The 16 different lamps are realized with industrial raw piping elements and designed to
illuminate the paths to and from the climbing refuge without causing light pollution.
The lamps are made to withstand the weather as well as vandalism. XIX metal group realization - Idea and concept by Grex Portmann and Maja Thommen.
Design and realization by Uri Moss, Grex Portmann & M.Thommen in Sennhof, Switzerland. Mai 2017: The lamps are now mounted in the Kalandraka.

projects.title: Apocalyptic Fence
projects.bodytext_html:
Custom fencing for the 'Apocalyptic Zen Beer Garden' of the new White Trash Fast Food
restaurant in Berlin Treptow, embedding one fully stripped coach and three upright
standing car wrecks, May 2014.

Concept by Wally, White Trash Fast Food.
Design and realisation together with Horst Steel, Stahlrichter, Marco Schöne and Uri Moss.
Flamethrowers by Eddie Egal.

projects.title: The Fifth Estate - Film Furniture
projects.bodytext_html:
Realization of the rough and sculpture-like furniture for the 'Tacheles scene' in the
thriller based on real events around Julian Assange and Daniel Domscheit-Berg,
directed by Bill Condon. The sitting area, consisting of 4 chairs, 1 sofa, 1 table and 6 lamps was realised
together with KAI /D and Stahlrichter /D, January 2013, Berlin, Germany.

projects.title: The Kiss Machine
projects.bodytext_html:
The Kiss Machine mechanism is based on an articulating, electric train arm.  The 'lips' rested on a pivot point between the wheels allowing the operator to articulate the extension arm out with a simple lever. The mobile machine was designed specifically for this spectacle, searching for the interaction of actor and spectator. Concept and construction together with Marco Collabucci /I.
Realized in the context of 'Wheel of Power', a theatrical production in an empty train factory,
staged by Derevo /RU for the 400th anniversary of the city of Mannheim /D, 2007

projects.title: The 17 ton Bar
projects.bodytext_html:
The base for this massive bar was made from the recycled, one hundred year old, steel
girders of gate 17 of Zurich's main train station.
The 17 ton Bar was installed at the Zoom Festival and was accompanied by a mad 'art car'
and pyrotechnics performance in 1997.

projects.title: The Torso, a machine performance
projects.bodytext_html:
The Torso was a celebration of the amazing work machines which are still in use on the
Russian scrapyard Bto Met: Especially interesting was the twelve meter tall wooden tower
on rails.Meant for brute crushing, it houses an immense metal weight which simply falls
from this height onto the scrap. A fascinating and raw system to flatten cast metal parts. The group made a solid metal torso which was lowered by a magnetic crane into the crushing
ditch. Then the wooden tower drove over the ditch. Falling from ten meters in height, the
two-ton iron globe crushed the torso completely. The whole performance was accompanied
by the stunning sounds of the machines.

projects.title: The Iron Channel
projects.bodytext_html:
This first largescale group work of XIX was realized in the context of the multimedia event
Eurokot. 7 tons of scrap were welded into a 10 meters long installation, including sound
machines and light effects, in one arm of the pedestrian underpass Escherwyss Unterführung,
Zurich /CH
